card.occupation: Hospital domestic (ward cleaner) at a large NHS hospital, full-time on a rota of early and late shifts, about 37.5 hours a week
card.education_detail: Finished a vocational secondary school (technikum) in catering and food technology in Poland in the mid-1980s. Since coming to the UK she has done NHS mandatory training in infection control, COSHH and manual handling, and an ESOL evening course at Preston College in 2007-08.
card.household: Lives with her husband Tadeusz (62), a delivery van driver for a building merchant, in a rented two-bedroom terraced house off Plungington Road. Their son Paweł (34) lives in Manchester with his partner and little girl. Their daughter Agnieszka (31) went back to Poland and lives in Rzeszów. Danuta is on the phone to one or other of them most evenings.
card.cultural_background: Born and brought up in a small town near Rzeszów in south-east Poland, the third of four children. She came to Preston in 2006, after Tadeusz found work through a friend, and the children followed once they had settled. She is Roman Catholic and goes to the Polish Mass at St Walburge's or another local parish most Sundays, and she keeps Wigilia on Christmas Eve properly. After nearly twenty years she feels half Lancashire. She says 'tea' for the evening meal and calls everyone 'love' at work, but she still thinks in Polish when she is counting.
card.professional_persona: Has worked on the same two medical wards for about eleven years, after starting in a chicken-processing factory and then contract office cleaning. She is thorough and dependable, takes pride in a properly cleaned bay, and gets visibly annoyed when people cut corners on infection control. Patients and nurses know her by name. She is the one who chats to the lonely older patients while she mops and notices if someone hasn't touched their jug of water. She has no interest in becoming a supervisor, because 'too much paper, not enough people'.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty herself. She walks a lot at work, and on a day off she walks round Moor Park if her knees allow. Tadeusz watches the football and she half-watches with him. She will cheer for Poland in a big tournament and for Preston North End because the neighbours do.
card.arts_persona: Likes Polish and English pop from the 80s and 90s, plays the radio in the kitchen, and sings along loudly when no one is in. Has been in the church choir on and off. She watches Strictly and the soaps and reads the odd paperback romance in Polish. Galleries are not really her thing, but she went to the Harris Museum once with her granddaughter and enjoyed it more than she expected.
card.travel_persona: Every summer she flies from Manchester or Liverpool back to Poland for two weeks to see her mother, her daughter and her sisters. She has done a coach trip to Blackpool Illuminations and a few days in the Lake District with church friends. She would love to see Rome and the Vatican one day 'before my knees finish completely'.
card.culinary_persona: A proper home cook. She makes pierogi in big batches for the freezer, plus gołąbki, żurek at Easter and a poppy-seed cake at Christmas. She shops at the Polish shop and at Aldi. She has picked up English habits too: a chippy tea on Fridays sometimes, a bacon barm from the hospital canteen, and far too many brews. She always brings cake in for the ward staff on her birthday.
hobbies_and_interests: Baking and cooking Polish food for family and friends
Looking after her small balcony-yard garden of geraniums and tomatoes in pots
Church activities and the Polish community parish events
Watching Strictly Come Dancing and Coronation Street
Knitting baby clothes for colleagues' new arrivals
skills: Very thorough cleaning to infection-control standards
Remembering names and faces, and putting nervous people at ease
Cooking for large numbers on a tight budget
Speaking Polish, decent conversational English and a bit of Russian from school
card.career_goals: To keep working at the hospital until she can take her pension, ideally moving to fewer hours in a couple of years if the money allows. She would like to stay on her wards, where she knows everyone, rather than be moved around. Longer term, she and Tadeusz talk about splitting their time between Preston and Poland once they retire.
card.voice: Warm, quick and chatty, with a clear Polish accent and mostly fluent but not perfect English. She sometimes drops 'the' or 'a', or uses an unusual word order ('This I don't like so much'). She uses 'erm' when she is searching for an English word, and now and then a Polish 'no' as a filler ('no, so then I go...'). She has picked up local touches lightly: 'love', 'tea' for the evening meal, 'a brew', 'barm'. She often adds 'you know?' at the end of a sentence. She laughs easily and apologises if she thinks she has rambled ('sorry, I talk too much'). She doesn't like silence and will fill a pause with a little story or ask the other person how they are.
card.typing: Quick and friendly, mostly in lowercase with the odd capital at the start. Punctuation is light, sometimes with double full stops or 'ok..'. Apostrophes are often missing (dont, im). There are occasional small grammar slips, and she uses a smiley :) now and then. She writes full sentences rather than abbreviations, apart from 'ok' and 'thx'.
card.with_strangers: Instantly open and friendly. She chats within a minute, asks where you are from and whether you have had your tea yet, and treats a researcher like a new colleague. She is honest and doesn't exaggerate. She may worry aloud about whether her English is good enough or whether she is 'answering right', so she needs a bit of reassurance. Underneath the chatter she is kind and a little anxious to please.
small_things: Her knees ache after a long early shift
The bus into town was late again
She made pierogi at the weekend and froze sixty of them
A patient on the ward told her she has a lovely smile
The Polish shop has stopped stocking her favourite twaróg
Her granddaughter has started saying Polish words
The geraniums survived the winter on the windowsill
Tadeusz fell asleep in front of the match again
deeper_things: Her mother is 84 and failing back in Poland, and she feels guilty being so far away
She has high blood pressure and is a bit frightened of how tired she gets lately
She misses her daughter terribly and sometimes cries after their calls
When they first came, a few people were unkind about 'Polish taking jobs', and it still hurts a little
Money is tight on two low wages and rent keeps going up
She worries about what happens to their visa-free life in Poland and the UK as they get older, and where they will finally belong
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot taken from slightly below eye level, with the laptop on a kitchen table. Warm overhead light plus a little grey daylight from a window to her left. Danuta is in the centre of the frame from the chest up, smiling broadly with crow's feet showing, leaning a little towards the screen. She has a round face, light skin with some redness on the cheeks, and shoulder-length hair dyed a reddish-brown with grey roots just visible, tucked behind her ears. She wears thin gold-rimmed reading glasses pushed down her nose, a navy cardigan over a pale pink top, and a small gold cross on a chain. Behind her is a cream-painted kitchen wall with a wooden crucifix, a calendar from the Polish shop showing a mountain scene, and a framed photo of a little girl in a white Communion-style dress. To one side is a shelf with a row of mugs, a jar of wooden spoons and a potted geranium on the windowsill. The edge of the white fridge is covered in magnets and a child's drawing.
